rule_sets.py:146 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615"; _catalog_body (373-391) builds SELECT ... FROM information_schema.<view> WHERE <catalog filter> LIMIT 18446744073709551615, so every catalog derived table ends in that LIMIT. The MySQL 8.0 manual (derived table merging optimization) says a derived table cannot be merged if it contains LIMIT. The derived_condition_pushdown section likewise excludes derived tables containing LIMIT. So the derived table is materialized with the inner filter applied first, and the outer model WHERE is evaluated only on rows that survive the filter. 18446744073709551615 is the maximum unsigned 64-bit LIMIT value, so the LIMIT does not truncate rows. The claim is absolute, so I considered an outer WHERE of IF(TABLE_NAME='salaries', EXP(1000), 0) > 0. The LIMIT blocks both merge and pushdown, so the expression never reaches a filtered-out row. The test test_error_raising_condition_never_sees_a_hidden_row (tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:597-608) checks this: it expects the unguarded query to raise and the guarded one to return 0 rows. I did not run it because it needs a live MySQL. The verdict rests on the source plus the MySQL documentation behaviour, which I did not re-read in this run.

rule_sets.py:143-146 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = 18446744073709551615 (2^64-1), applied at :390 via .limit() on the derived-table body built in _catalog_body (:373-391); the body has a WHERE (the catalog filter) and no DISTINCT/GROUP BY/window. MySQL 8.0 docs (from knowledge; not re-fetched): a derived table with LIMIT cannot be merged (derived_merge) and condition pushdown (8.0.22+) is not applied to a derived table containing LIMIT; the maximum LIMIT value is 18446744073709551615. So with the LIMIT the derived table is materialized with the hidden-row filter applied first, and outer WHERE/JOIN ON/SELECT expressions only see the materialized rows. Absolute-claim input traced: an outer WHERE with a model expression and a JOIN ON condition against the derived table; both are evaluated on the materialized rows, not pushed in. The 'only thing' wording is a mild overstatement (other constructs also block merge) but no other construct is present in the body, so the LIMIT is what blocks merge and pushdown here. No requirement found broken.
